description: DPS (Dynamic Potential Search) finds a path that costs at most `w` times the optimum (it is *bounded-suboptimal*). It needs one *admissible* heuristic `h`, which never overestimates the remaining cost. Among the open states with `f = g + h ≤ w · f_min`, where `f_min` is the smallest `f` that is open, it expands the state with the largest *potential* `(w · f_min − g) / h`: the state most likely to lead to a solution within the bound. The potential changes when `f_min` changes, so the crate groups the open states by their `(g, h)` pair and scans the groups at each expansion. Use it for bounded-suboptimal search when you have no second estimate, in particular with small integer edge costs.

papers.authors: Daniel Gilon, Ariel Felner, Roni Stern
papers.title: Dynamic Potential Search — A New Bounded Suboptimal Search
